assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Hydroxide ion, OH⁻
items.clue: The ion present in aqueous solutions of alkalis; it is what makes a solution alkaline.

items.label: Hydrogen ion, H⁺
items.clue: The ion that all acids produce in aqueous solution; it is what makes a solution acidic.

items.label: End point
items.clue: The moment when the indicator changes colour permanently, showing that the acid and alkali have exactly reacted.

items.label: Pipette
items.clue: Apparatus that delivers an accurate fixed volume, used with a safety filler to place the alkali in the conical flask.

questions.stem: Which equation correctly represents the reaction of zinc with dilute sulfuric acid?

options.text: Zn + H₂SO₄ → ZnSO₄ + H₂O
Zn + 2H₂SO₄ → ZnSO₄ + 2H₂
Zn + H₂SO₄ → ZnSO₄ + H₂
Zn + H₂SO₄ → ZnSO₄ + H

questions.explanation: Sulfuric acid produces sulfates and the hydrogen is released as H₂. The equation is balanced as written.

questions.stem: Calcium ions are Ca²⁺ and nitrate ions are NO₃⁻. What is the formula of calcium nitrate?

options.text: CaNO₃
Ca(NO₃)₂
Ca₂(NO₃)₂
Ca(NO₃)(NO₃)

questions.explanation: Two nitrate ions are needed to balance the 2+ charge on one calcium ion, and the bracket shows that both are nitrate ions.

questions.stem: Four solutions have pH values of 2, 7, 9 and 13. Which statement is correct?

options.text: The solution at pH 2 must be alkaline and pH 13 acidic
The solution at pH 7 does not contain any ions
The solutions at pH 9 and pH 13 are both neutral
The solution at pH 2 is acidic and pH 13 is alkaline

questions.explanation: Solutions with a pH below 7 are acidic and those above 7 are alkaline, so pH 2 is acidic and pH 13 alkaline.

questions.stem: What is measured in a titration between an acid and an alkali?

options.text: The mass of salt made when they are mixed
The temperature rise during the reaction
The exact pH at every stage of the reaction
The volumes of the solutions that react together

questions.explanation: Titration measures the volumes of acid and alkali solutions that react with each other, using a suitable indicator.

questions.stem: In a reaction between an acid and a base, where does the positive ion in the salt come from?

options.text: From the acid that is being used
From the water formed in the reaction
From the indicator that has been added
From the base, alkali or carbonate used

questions.explanation: The acid supplies the negative ion of the salt and the base, alkali or carbonate supplies the positive metal ion.

questions.stem: Which equation represents the neutralisation of an acid by an alkali?

options.text: H⁺ + OH⁻ → H₂O
H⁺ + OH⁻ → H₂O₂
2H⁺ + 2OH⁻ → H₂O
H⁺ + OH⁻ → H₂

questions.explanation: In neutralisation between an acid and an alkali, hydrogen ions react with hydroxide ions to produce water.

questions.stem: Why is a single indicator such as phenolphthalein used in a titration rather than universal indicator?

options.text: It shows the pH at every stage of the titration
It changes colour sharply at the end point
Universal indicator reacts with the acid used
It makes the neutralisation happen faster

questions.explanation: A single indicator gives one sudden colour change, so the end point can be judged to the nearest drop.

questions.stem: Calcium carbonate chips are dropped into dilute nitric acid and the mixture fizzes. What are the three products?

options.text: Calcium nitrate and water, no gas
Calcium nitrate, water and hydrogen
Calcium nitrate, water and carbon dioxide
Calcium nitrite, water and CO₂ gas

questions.explanation: Metal carbonates neutralise acids to produce a salt, water and carbon dioxide; nitric acid produces nitrates.

questions.stem: Which statement about the pH scale is correct?

options.text: It runs from 1 to 14 and measures the acid strength
It runs from 0 to 7 for acids and no further
It runs from 0 to 14 and measures acidity or alkalinity
It runs from 0 to 14 and measures concentration

questions.explanation: The pH scale, from 0 to 14, is a measure of the acidity or alkalinity of a solution.

questions.stem: In Required practical 2, a student records titres of 24.10, 23.55 and 23.60 cm³. What should be done next?

options.text: Take the mean of all three titres recorded
Use the largest titre, because it is safest
Average the two concordant titres only
Repeat until the titres are all identical

questions.explanation: The rough first titre is discarded and the mean is taken from the titres that agree within 0.10 cm³.

questions.stem: Copper(II) oxide is added to warm dilute sulfuric acid. What is produced?

options.text: Copper sulfate and water only
Copper sulfate, water and hydrogen
Copper sulfate and carbon dioxide
Copper sulfide and water vapour

questions.explanation: A metal oxide is a base, and acids are neutralised by bases to produce a salt and water only.

questions.stem: A few drops of universal indicator are added to a solution and the colour is matched to a chart. What does this give?

options.text: An exact pH value, correct to two decimal places
An approximate value for the solution's pH
The concentration of the acid in mol per dm³
The volume of alkali needed for neutralisation

questions.explanation: Universal indicator, a wide range indicator, gives an approximate pH when its colour is matched to a chart.

questions.stem: (HT) The pH of a solution falls from 5 to 3. How does the hydrogen ion concentration change?

options.text: It increases by a factor of 2
It increases by a factor of 1000
It increases by a factor of ten only
It increases by a factor of 100

questions.explanation: Each fall of one pH unit multiplies the hydrogen ion concentration by 10, so a fall of two units multiplies it by 100.

questions.stem: (HT) Equal concentrations of hydrochloric acid and ethanoic acid are compared. Which has the lower pH, and why?

options.text: Hydrochloric acid, as it fully ionises
Ethanoic acid, as it ionises only partly
Hydrochloric acid, as it is more concentrated
Neither, as their concentrations are equal

questions.explanation: For a given concentration, the stronger acid produces more hydrogen ions, so it has the lower pH.

questions.stem: (HT) Solution X has pH 4 and solution Y has pH 7. What can be said about their hydrogen ion concentrations?

options.text: X has just 3 times the hydrogen ion concentration of Y
Y has the higher hydrogen ion concentration here
X has 1000 times the hydrogen ion concentration of Y
Both are neutral, so the two values must match

questions.explanation: Three pH units below neutral means the hydrogen ion concentration is 10 × 10 × 10 = 1000 times greater.
